OpenKeyID · Matching Framework

Client–Assistant Personality Matching

Which assistant personality best fits which client. The model is complementary fit — the strongest assistant covers the client's blind spots rather than mirroring their strengths — applied in two layers: the archetype family grid first, then Big Five (OCEAN) trait rules to refine. Each family carries its signature gemstone.

THE CORE IDEADrivers pair with Executors

Every archetype rolls up to one of eight trait families, each with its own gemstone. Four are drivers (they set direction and create momentum); four are executors (they deliver, stabilize, and care for people). In a client→assistant hierarchy, the reliable pattern is a driver client matched to an executor assistant — and vice-versa. Two drivers contest the wheel; two of the same family amplify a shared blind spot.

THE GEMSTONE SYSTEM8 base gems → 64 hybrid archetypes

Each archetype is a hybrid gemstone. The primary trait sets the base gem and family; the secondary trait fuses a second gem inside it — that fusion is the archetype. An Apex archetype (no strong secondary) stays a single pure gem. Eight base gems combine into all 64.

LAYER 2OCEAN trait refinement

Once the family pairing is set, tune with the Big Five. Two traits are complementary (the assistant covers), two match (align styles), one adapts within a band. These rules are drawn straight from the "ideal subordinate" guidance stored on each of the 243 OCEAN outcomes.

TraitRuleWhyTarget
CConscientiousnessCOMPLEMENT — assistant runs HighThe single biggest lever. Whatever the client scores, the assistant should be High-C: the "structural integrator" who turns intent into reliable, shipped work. The lift is largest when the client is Low-C (visionary/messy) and the assistant supplies all the structure.assistant C ≥ client C; aim High
NNeuroticismCOMPLEMENT — assistant runs LowStability is a universal assistant asset. A Low-N assistant absorbs pressure and creates psychological safety. Critical when the client is High-N (vigilant/anxious): they need a calm anchor, never a second worrier.assistant N ≤ client N; aim Low
EExtraversionMATCH — sync the energyHigh-E clients want a vocal, collaborative brainstorming partner; Low-E clients want quiet, asynchronous check-ins and protected focus. A mismatch reads as social friction on both sides.assistant E ≈ client E
AAgreeablenessMATCH — sync the conflict styleHigh-A clients want an empathetic, low-ego collaborator; Low-A clients want a direct operator who defends ideas in friction-heavy debate. Match this axis so their communication values align.assistant A ≈ client A
OOpennessADAPT — within one bandKeep the assistant within ±1 band of the client. For a High-O client who loves radical pivots, the assistant should be adaptable (Med–High O) and High-C so novelty still ships. Low-O clients want a playbook-loyal operator.assistant O within ±1 of client O

Stabilizer Tourmaline
Executor who ships the vision and stays calm.
  1. Family (Layer 1): Catalyst client → Stabilizer is Ideal (the "structural integrator"); Analyzer is Strong. Avoid another Catalyst.
  2. C — complement: client is Low-C, so the assistant must be High-C — this is the biggest single fit driver.
  3. N — complement: client is High-N, so the assistant should be Low-N to anchor them.
  4. E & A — match: client is High-E / Low-A → assistant High-E, Low-A, so energy and direct conflict-style align.
  5. O — adapt: client is High-O → assistant Med–High-O so they keep pace with pivots without adding chaos.
OpenKeyID Client–Assistant Matching Guide — v1. Layer 1 grid derived from the operational dynamics of the 64 trait-list archetypes; Layer 2 rules derived from the ideal-manager / ideal-subordinate fields on the 243 Big Five outcomes. The Pairing Explorer scores every pairing as 3×(primary↔primary) + (primary↔secondary) + (secondary↔primary) + ½(secondary↔secondary). Gemstone artwork pulled from the live OpenKeyID outcome records. A design framework to validate against real placement outcomes before wiring it into the app — ratings are directional (client→assistant), not symmetric.
